findings.text: the plan adds escalated_shortlist as "the one cut of a source's shortlist plus its §11 siblings", but the cut already exists: candidates.py's route materialises shortlist = tuple(ordered[: limits.shortlist_size]) into Route.shortlist (imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:478,499), and §11 landed the widened set with each candidate's Jev rank and its cluster-sibling provenance persisted on the MAPPING_CANDIDATE edge itself (rank, arms = 'cluster'; described at imas_codex/graph/models.py:14562). After §8 the map stage reads those edges through read_candidates (already Jev-ordered, imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:576), so "top N plus §11 siblings" is a filter over output the stage already holds. The plan neither extends the candidates.py owner nor states why reading the ordered edges directly cannot serve the prompt, which risks a second shortlist-cut implementation drifting from the discover-stage one.

response_events.reason: The two cuts serve different inputs and rules, not one rule twice. route cuts in-memory PairJudgments at the candidate stage, top map-shortlist-size of every judgment, to decide whether a source escalates. escalated_shortlist cuts the persisted MAPPING_CANDIDATE edges for the reasoning prompt and keeps every cluster-arm sibling even beyond the top N, so cross-IDS homes reach the model. Both order by the same persisted Jev rank and read the same map-shortlist-size setting, so their order and size cannot drift; reading the ordered edges directly at the call site would just inline the sibling rule at two call sites (prompt and worker) instead of one helper.
